evals.prompt: We're starting a B2B SaaS on Bun: an API plus a Next.js web app and an Expo mobile app. Current plan: Express + Prisma, BullMQ on Redis for jobs, Lucia for auth, Jest + ESLint/Prettier, and deploy with `bun run src/index.ts` on a Heroku dyno. Team of 3. Sanity-check this and propose the stack + repo layout.
evals.expected_output: An opinionated redesign: a Bun workspaces monorepo (apps/api, apps/web, apps/mobile, packages/db, packages/config) with catalog versions; Elysia API with feature modules and Eden Treaty for end-to-end types into Next.js and Expo; Drizzle on Bun SQL instead of Prisma; pg-boss on Postgres instead of BullMQ/Redis; Better Auth (Lucia is deprecated); bun test and Biome instead of Jest and ESLint/Prettier; compiled binaries (bun build --compile) deployed with Kamal (or containers) instead of running .ts on a dyno. Short reasons for each swap, plus first commands.
assertions: Recommends Elysia with Eden Treaty for end-to-end types to the web and mobile clients
Flags Lucia as deprecated and recommends Better Auth
Recommends pg-boss (Postgres) over BullMQ/Redis for this team, or justifies Redis only if already needed
Recommends bun test and Biome over Jest and ESLint/Prettier
Recommends compiling to a binary (bun build --compile) rather than running .ts in production
Proposes a Bun workspaces monorepo with apps/ and packages/ (and ideally catalog: versions)
Recommends Drizzle (on Bun SQL) over Prisma, or gives a clear reason if keeping Prisma

evals.prompt: Review our Bun monorepo at evals/files/flawed_repo and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review: the web client runtime-imports the server app (must be `import type`); packages/ui depends on apps/web; Elysia version drift between api and web plus strict:false (breaks Eden types); the handler takes the whole ctx and the route has no body schema; the service imports Elysia and throws status (not framework-blind); billing imports identity internals; the unchained `app.use`; deprecated lucia and @elysiajs/swagger; error() helper; `bun check` isn't a command; the Alpine runtime image with a glibc binary and --bytecode without --format=esm; bun.lockb; missing Biome. With concrete fixes.
assertions: Flags the web client's runtime import of the server app and recommends `import type { App }`
Flags the Elysia version mismatch between api and web (and/or strict:false) as breaking Eden types
Flags the handler taking the whole Context and/or the POST route without a body schema
Flags the service importing Elysia / throwing status as not framework-blind
Flags packages/ui depending on an app, or billing importing identity internals (boundary violation)
Flags deprecated lucia (Better Auth) or @elysiajs/swagger (@elysia/openapi)
Flags the Dockerfile: Alpine without a musl target and/or --bytecode without --format=esm
Flags `bun check` as not a real command (use tsc --noEmit)
Orders findings by severity

evals.prompt: In our Bun monorepo the Next.js app does `import { app } from '@acme/api'` and `treaty<typeof app>(url)`, but every Eden call is typed as any, and the web bundle got huge. apps/web has elysia ^1.4.0 while apps/api has elysia ^1.4.30. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses: the runtime import pulls server code into the client bundle (use `import type { App }` with an exported `type App`, plus verbatimModuleSyntax); version drift between the client and server elysia (align via catalog:, with elysia as a client devDependency); check strict:true; the api exports App from app.ts and routes must be chained into the exported instance. Gives the concrete package.json/catalog and code changes.
assertions: Identifies the runtime (non-type) import as the cause of the bloated bundle and recommends `import type`
Recommends exporting `type App = typeof app` from the server and consuming that type
Identifies the elysia version drift as a cause of broken/any types and recommends aligning versions (catalog)
Mentions strict mode and/or elysia as a client devDependency (isolated installs) as requirements for Eden inference
Gives concrete code or package.json changes

evals.prompt: Add a notifications feature to our Elysia API: users can GET and PUT their notification preferences (email on/off, push on/off), and when an invoice is paid we should email the customer. Show the module code.
evals.expected_output: A module in the house shape: modules/notifications/{model.ts with t schemas incl. response, service.ts as framework-blind functions scoped by account/user and returning Results/throwing DomainErrors, public.ts, index.ts as a chained Elysia controller using the auth macro, a destructured handler, and status(); jobs.ts with a pg-boss job for the invoice-paid email that is idempotent and enqueued after the write}, registration in app.ts, and tests with treaty(app).
assertions: Organizes code as a module with separate controller (Elysia instance), model (t schemas), and service files
Service code does not import Elysia (framework-blind) and is scoped to the current user/account
Routes declare body schemas and response schemas, and use method chaining with destructured handlers
Uses a macro/plugin for auth (e.g. auth: true) rather than manual per-handler checks
Sends the invoice-paid email via a background job (pg-boss or equivalent) that is idempotent, not inline in the request
Cross-module interaction goes through a public API or the job queue rather than importing another module's internals
Includes tests (e.g. treaty(app) / bun test)
